title: Leon Bridges Tries a New Sound on 'Happiness Anytime'
summary:
Leon Bridges became known in 2015 with his first album, Coming Home. Its retro-soul and R&B songs became his signature sound. Eleven years later, he is trying something new. His fifth studio album is called Happiness Anytime. It brings in Afrobeats, Brazilian music and disco.

On the new album, Bridges uses a live band and electronic sounds instead of mostly playing acoustic guitar. He hopes the music will make people dance. “That's what was beautiful about this album. We didn't know what we wanted to make going into it,” he told Morning Edition. “But, you know, it was all about cultivating a new sound. And I felt that.”

Bridges says the album shows his journey as he becomes a more complex musician. He talked with NPR's Michel Martin about finding joy in different cultures and about growing since his early career. For him, reinvention is the big idea: do not just repeat the old style, but mix in sounds from around the world.
why_it_matters: Trying new things instead of always repeating what worked before is how artists — and everyone — keep growing.
